name: Sculpfun E1 12W
tagline: Enclosed 12W CoreXY diode with camera and air pump for $499
tldr: The Sculpfun E1 is the entry version of the E1 line: the same Class 1 enclosure, CoreXY gantry, 400 × 320 mm work area, camera, air pump and honeycomb bed as the E1 Pro, with a 12W diode. Sculpfun claims 8 mm wood in one pass and 600 mm/s engraving. A Dual bundle adds a swappable 3W IR module. Launched June 2026.
mainObjective: Affordable enclosed engraving with light wood cutting on a mid-size bed

priceRange.note: $499 single 12W, $949 Dual with 3W IR module (Sculpfun store, Oct 2026)

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cut: Basswood & plywood up to 8 mm (claimed, one pass)
cannot: Objects taller than 42 mm (30 mm with honeycomb)

pros: Optional 3W infrared module fits the same machine for metal marking
Sculpfun claims 8 mm wood in a single pass
Fills at ~70–180 mm/s in our benchmarks, up to 600 mm/s top speed
cons: Cutting is slower than on the E1 Pro: a 3 mm basswood square takes ~5–8 min
Adding the IR module later costs $499, more than the price gap to the Dual kit
Thick plywood still means several passes and longer jobs than the spec sheet suggests
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 12W E1 in the Sculpfun E1 line. It suits engraving-first users who want an enclosure and a decent bed without spending $800+. Compare it with the 21W E1 Pro if you know you will cut wood every week: it is worth the extra $350.
proTips: Use several moderate passes rather than one slow pass for 5 mm+ wood. Keep the air pump on for cuts. Check focus manually before each job and remove the honeycomb for thicker objects.

faq.question: What does the Sculpfun E1 12W cut in one pass?
faq.answer: Sculpfun claims 8 mm of wood in a single pass. In our benchmarks a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes about 5–8 min at 4–9 mm/s. Thin dark acrylic works; clear acrylic does not, because the blue beam passes through it.

faq.question: Is the Dual version worth $450 more?
faq.answer: The Dual adds the 3W infrared module for marking metal and some plastics: $949 against $499 for the single 12W on Sculpfun's store (October 2026). The IR3 module alone costs $499, so if you already know you want metal marking, the Dual saves about $50 over adding it later.

faq.question: E1 12W or E1 Pro 21W: which should I choose?
faq.answer: The 12W suits engraving-led gifts and small batches, and costs $350 less ($499 against $849). The Pro claims 12 mm instead of 8 mm in one pass and cuts our 3 mm square in about 3–5 min instead of 5–8. If you cut plywood every week, the Pro pays back; if you mostly engrave, keep the difference.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 12W E1 is the budget door into the E1 enclosure: for $499 you get the camera, air pump, CoreXY gantry and a 400 × 320 mm bed, which is large for an enclosed machine at this price. Engraving quality on wood, leather and stone does not depend much on the extra watts.
editorialDepth.limitations: Cutting is where the 12W shows its limits against the E1 Pro: more passes, slower jobs. Clearance is shallow, focus is manual, and like every diode it cannot cut clear acrylic.

standoutFeatures.title: Enclosed with camera for $499
standoutFeatures.body: Enclosure, camera and air pump at the entry price, where many enclosed diodes start well above it.

standoutFeatures.title: Infrared add-on
standoutFeatures.body: The IR3 3W infrared module ($499) fits the E1 for metal and plastic marking, or comes in the $949 Dual kit.

standoutFeatures.title: Fast CoreXY motion
standoutFeatures.body: Rated at 36,000 mm/min (600 mm/s): fills of roughly 70–180 mm/s in our tests keep engraving jobs short.
